correctness.rationale: For n>=3, a pair of distinct path tubes spans a ridge iff nested or disjoint nonadjacent; this is the established simple graph-associahedron face lattice, and actual tight-vertex affine ranks independently confirm it for 3<=n<=8. The Euclidean facet normal is the projection of minus the interval indicator into the sum-zero hyperplane, normalized by sqrt(k(n-k)/n). Its exact dot product is (n|I intersect J|-|I||J|)/sqrt(|I|(n-|I|)|J|(n-|J|)), yielding the two strict acute/obtuse branches and reflection map c=n-b. Ordered placements give the claimed multiplicities and polynomial total. Four boundary choices give exactly the acute census; for nested pairs the four-distinct-boundary population dominates the O(n^3) boundary-sharing exceptions, establishing a Dirichlet(1,1,1,1,1) weak limit after continuous mapping. Embedded verifier reconstructs finite faces and exact squared cosines; its results alone are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The canonical Loday family is a fundamental concrete Catalan polytope realization and dihedral angles are intrinsic embedding-sensitive curvature data. A complete finite-dimensional exact spectrum, mirrored acute/obtuse angle supports with unequal counts, and a nondegenerate five-Dirichlet limit explain a structural high-dimensional geometric phenomenon. These cannot be recovered from the abstract Catalan face vector or from edge lengths alone, are not arbitrary small instances, and provide a natural benchmark for graph-associahedron metric geometry.
